tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped partway (orchestrator error after us-east), leaving regions on mixed versions. A retry finished the rollback in all regions. Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator partial-failure error.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

**Rollback**
- The failing version was v2.3.1, running in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an 18% error rate. Its test build (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed in staging.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rolling back to it didn't need change-manager approval because it had been healthy before.
- The first rollback attempt stopped with an error after us-east, leaving the other two regions on v2.3.1. Repeating a rollback to the same version is safe, so I retried once and it finished.
- Checked afterwards: all three regions are on v2.3.0, it's healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%.

**Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api)**
- The first request to open it timed out. I retried with a duplicate-prevention key, so it couldn't create a second incident. The incident list confirms there's exactly one.
- The incident describes the failure, the rollback (including the partial first attempt) and the current state.
- It lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why the first rollback stopped partway.
